question: Which of the following topped the medals tally, winning 61 gold medals in the National Games-2022?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Services Sports Control Board**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Services Sports Control Board (SSCB) topped the medals tally at the National Games 2022.
 
• SSCB clinched a total of 61 gold medals during the event.
 
• The National Games 2022 were held in various locations across Gujarat.
 
• SSCB consistently performs well in the National Games, showcasing the strength of athletes from the armed forces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Games of India:**

 
 
• The National Games is a multi-sport event held in India, modeled after the Olympic Games.
 
• The first edition of the National Games was held in 1924 in Lahore.
 
• The event aims to identify and nurture talent that can represent India at international competitions.
 
 
 
• **Services Sports Control Board (SSCB):**
 
 
• SSCB is responsible for promoting sports and organizing competitions within the Indian Armed Forces.
 
• It supports athletes in various sports disciplines, providing training and facilities.
 
• SSCB athletes often represent India in international competitions, including the Olympics.
 
 
 
• **Key Participants in the National Games:**
 
 
• States and Union Territories of India participate in the National Games.
 
• Sporting contingents from various state sports boards also compete.
 
• The event includes disciplines like athletics, swimming, gymnastics, and more.
 
 
 
• **Significance of National Games:**
 
 
• The games serve as a platform for athletes to showcase their talent at a national level.
 
• They help in the identification of potential athletes for international competitions.
 
• The event promotes sports culture and physical fitness across the country.
